name: Fruit-and-honey diet
lead: The fruit-and-honey diet is a sugar-forward way of eating built mainly on fruit and honey, close to fruitarianism. People in the looksmaxxing and wellness spaces adopt it chasing clearer skin, a lean look and a "clean" body, often framing fruit as a cleansing, easily digested fuel.[1]

Fruitarianism itself is a diet of mainly fruit, sometimes with nuts and seeds, and variants may add honey, olive oil or dried fruit.[1] Honey is mostly fructose and glucose and is about as sweet as table sugar.[2] No studies of a combined fruit-and-honey diet have been found.

chain: Diet built on fruit and honey
High intake of water-rich, easily digested foods
Followers report a lighter, cleaner look
angle.text: Followers eat mainly fruit and honey in the belief it supports clear skin and a lean physique. The claims are practitioner reports.

paras: Fruitarian diets vary: some include only fruit that falls naturally, while others add legumes, honey, olive oil or dried fruit.[1] Motives include ethical, religious, environmental and perceived health reasons, such as removing supposed toxins.[1]
Honey provides about 43 kilocalories per tablespoon and has a water content of around 15.5 to 18 percent.[2]

Health experts cited in general references note possible shortfalls in protein, calcium, iron, zinc, vitamin D, B vitamins and essential fatty acids, and that fruit has no reliable natural source of vitamin B12.[1] High fruit sugar intake is a concern for people with diabetes or prediabetes and for tooth decay.[1] Nutritionists generally consider strict versions unsuitable for children, teenagers and nursing mothers.[1]
Honey is generally safe in typical food amounts, should not be given to infants under one year because of botulism risk, and may interact with diabetes and anticoagulant medications.[2]
No studies found. Honey has been studied for wound healing, burns and cough in other contexts.[2]

card.summary: A sugar-forward diet built on fruit and honey, followed for clear skin and a lean, light look.
card.note: Nutrient gaps (protein, B12, iron) and dental and blood-sugar concerns are noted for fruit-based diets.

quick.overview:
This is a diet centred on fruit and honey, a variant of fruitarianism. Followers report it as a cleansing, easily digested way of eating that supports clear skin and a lean look.

No studies have tested the specific fruit-and-honey combination.
quick.mechanism: Followers eat mostly fruit and honey, supplying sugars and water-rich foods in place of other food groups.
quick.risks: Health experts note possible gaps in protein, calcium, iron, zinc and B12, plus dental and blood-sugar concerns. Honey should not be given to infants under one.
